slides.body: Welcome back to Git and GitHub Deep Mastery.
A wrong rebase: the entry in the branch reflog below "rebase (finish)".
Two of the five have a root-cause box, and both boxes are about recipes that work in one situation and do damage in the next.

slides.body: Three ideas decide every case today.

slides.headline: First: which log
slides.body: The branch reflog has one line per operation on that branch.

slides.headline: Second: published or not
slides.body: Before a push, you may move the branch back.

rows: In progress, with conflicts you do not want to resolve
git reset --keep ORIG_HEAD, or the branch reflog
git revert -m 1 <merge>, and know the re-merge problem

slides.headline: Third: the lowest-risk move
slides.body: 🟡 CAUTION: git reset --keep <id> moves the branch and the files in the same way as --hard, and refuses if that would overwrite an uncommitted change.

slides.direction: The first root-cause box of section 13.8.
slides.text:
Observed behavior : "git reset --hard HEAD~1" after a merge leaves two of the three merged commits on main;
                    "git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD" then brings the third one back
Git state         : the merge was a fast-forward: main moved from 0529d31 to deec1c6 along three commits,
                    and no merge commit was created
Mechanism         : HEAD~1 is the first parent of the tip. After a true merge that is the previous tip of
                    main. After a fast-forward it is the previous commit of the branch that was merged.
                    The first reset wrote ORIG_HEAD = deec1c6, so the second one returned to the merged state
Root cause        : the recipe assumes a merge commit, and "ORIG_HEAD" was used two commands late
Why Git does this : a fast-forward only moves a ref (Chapter 8); there is nothing to mark where it started
                    except the reflog and, for one command, ORIG_HEAD
Correct fix       : read "git reflog show main" and reset to the entry below the merge line
Prevention        : undo a merge with ORIG_HEAD immediately, or by reflog entry; never by counting parents

slides.direction: The second root-cause box of section 13.8.
slides.text:
Observed behavior : after "git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD" the release branch shows the history of main,
                    and the release-only commit "Pin dependencies for 2.1" is gone
Git state         : ORIG_HEAD = f028350, written days earlier by a fast-forward merge on main
Mechanism         : git cherry-pick does not write ORIG_HEAD (section 13.5), so the slot held a value from
                    another operation on another branch; the reset moved release/2.1 to that commit
Root cause        : ORIG_HEAD was used as "undo the last command"; it means "before the last reset,
                    merge, rebase or am"
Why Git does this : ORIG_HEAD is one file with no notion of which branch or which command it belongs to
Correct fix       : git reflog show release/2.1, then reset --keep to the entry below the cherry-pick
Prevention        : undo by reflog entry; check "git log -1 ORIG_HEAD" before every use of ORIG_HEAD

"Undo the last merge" with HEAD~1. Root cause: a fast-forward creates no merge commit, so HEAD~1 is a commit of the merged branch, not the previous tip.
Resetting a rebased branch to its old tip when work was added afterwards. Root cause: the new commit sits on the rebased commits; anchor both tips and transplant the new commit with --onto.
Moving main back before copying the misplaced commits. Root cause: after the reset only the reflog names them; copy first, remove second.
Rewinding a shared branch to remove a pushed merge or pick. Root cause: others have the commits and will bring them back or diverge; add a revert instead.

slides.lead: Let's land this. You should now be able to say:
items: After a rebase, the old tip is the entry below "rebase (finish)" in the branch reflog; work added later is transplanted with --onto.

Commits on the wrong branch are copied first and removed second.

I check git log -1 ORIG_HEAD before every use of it, and I prefer git reset --keep.

slides.body: Read the rest of section 13.8 in Chapter 13. Do Lab 12.5, "A bad merge", Lab 12.7, "Lost work in detached HEAD", and Lab 12.9, "A wrong cherry-pick", in lab-manual/m12-recovery.md.
Today you undid five accidents by reading the right log.

beats.text: An engineer cherry-picks the wrong commit onto a release branch. A cherry-pick copies one commit's change onto the current branch. He remembers a recipe: git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD undoes the last operation. He runs it. Git answers with a commit subject that is exactly the fix he meant to pick. It looks like success.
beats.tele: An engineer cherry-picks the wrong commit onto a release branch. A cherry-pick copies one commit's change onto the current branch. He remembers a recipe: `git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` undoes the last operation. He runs it. Git answers with a commit subject that is exactly the fix he meant to pick. It looks like success.

beats.text: It's not. The release branch now shows the history of main. The commit that pins the dependencies for the release is gone from it. The only visible sign is one missing file. If nobody notices, the next release build resolves unpinned dependencies. Remember that missing file.
beats.tele: It's not. The release branch now shows the history of `main`. The commit that pins the dependencies for the release is gone from it. The only visible sign is one missing file. If nobody notices, the next release build resolves unpinned dependencies. Remember that missing file.

beats.text: The command did what it says. The engineer believed that ORIG_HEAD means "before the last command". It means "before the last reset, merge, rebase or am", on whatever branch that was.
beats.tele: The command did what it says. The engineer believed that `ORIG_HEAD` means "before the last command". It means "before the last reset, merge, rebase or am", on whatever branch that was.

beats.text: Welcome back to Git and GitHub Deep Mastery. Pull up a chair. In the previous video you learned the eight-step method and used it on three accidents. Today, five more, all with committed work, all recoverable. Each is the same method with a different ref to consult.
beats.tele: Welcome back to Git and GitHub Deep Mastery. Pull up a chair. In the previous video you learned the eight-step method and used it on three accidents. Today, five more, all with committed work, all recoverable. Each is the same method with a different ref to consult.

beats.text: A wrong rebase: the entry in the branch reflog below "rebase (finish)". A reflog is the local log of where a name pointed. A bad merge: the entry below the merge line. Commits on the wrong branch: the difference between main and origin/main. Detached HEAD, where you commit on no branch: the HEAD reflog, or git fsck. A wrong cherry-pick: the branch reflog again.
beats.tele: A wrong rebase: the entry in the branch reflog below "rebase (finish)". A reflog is the local log of where a name pointed. A bad merge: the entry below the merge line. Commits on the wrong branch: the difference between `main` and `origin/main`. Detached HEAD, where you commit on no branch: the HEAD reflog, or `git fsck`. A wrong cherry-pick: the branch reflog again.

beats.text: Two of the five have a root-cause box, and both boxes are about recipes that work in one situation and do damage in the next.
beats.tele: Two of the five have a root-cause box, and both boxes are about recipes that work in one situation and do damage in the next.

beats.text: return a branch to its state before a rebase when ORIG_HEAD is stale;
beats.tele: return a branch to its state before a rebase when `ORIG_HEAD` is stale;

beats.text: undo a merge that was not pushed and one that was;
beats.tele: undo a merge that was not pushed and one that was;

beats.text: move commits made on the wrong branch to the right one;
beats.tele: move commits made on the wrong branch to the right one;

beats.text: rescue commits left in detached HEAD;
beats.tele: rescue commits left in detached HEAD;

beats.text: remove a wrong cherry-pick without touching the commits around it.
beats.tele: remove a wrong cherry-pick without touching the commits around it.

beats.text: Three ideas decide every case today.
beats.tele: Three ideas decide every case today.

beats.text: First: which log. The branch reflog has one line per operation on that branch. A whole rebase is one entry, "rebase (finish)", and the line below it is the tip from before the rebase. A merge is one entry, and the line below it is where the branch was. That's the log you read when the question is "where was this branch". The HEAD reflog is the only log that sees detached HEAD.
beats.tele: First: which log. The branch reflog has one line per operation on that branch. A whole rebase is one entry, "rebase (finish)", and the line below it is the tip from before the rebase. A merge is one entry, and the line below it is where the branch was. That's the log you read when the question is "where was this branch". The HEAD reflog is the only log that sees detached HEAD.

beats.text: Second: published or not. Before a push, you may move the branch back. After a push to a branch that others have pulled, you don't rewind. You add commits, such as a revert, which undoes an earlier commit. For a merge the textbook gives a three-row table.
beats.tele: Second: published or not. Before a push, you may move the branch back. After a push to a branch that others have pulled, you don't rewind. You add commits, such as a revert, which undoes an earlier commit. For a merge the textbook gives a three-row table.

beats.text: The same split applies to a wrong cherry-pick and to commits on the wrong branch: reset before the push, revert after.
beats.tele: The same split applies to a wrong cherry-pick and to commits on the wrong branch: reset before the push, revert after.

beats.text: Third: the lowest-risk move. 🟡 CAUTION: git reset --keep <id> moves the branch and the files in the same way as --hard, and refuses if that would overwrite an uncommitted change. Use it wherever you would have typed --hard. And prefer copying to moving: with commits on the wrong branch, copy first, remove second.
beats.tele: Third: the lowest-risk move. 🟡 CAUTION: `git reset --keep <id>` moves the branch and the files in the same way as `--hard`, and refuses if that would overwrite an uncommitted change. Use it wherever you would have typed `--hard`. And prefer copying to moving: with commits on the wrong branch, copy first, remove second.

beats.text: When is ORIG_HEAD acceptable? Only as the very next command after the operation you want to undo, and only if that operation writes it. git cherry-pick doesn't. A commit doesn't. So a rebase followed by one commit, or a cherry-pick at any time, leaves ORIG_HEAD pointing somewhere you didn't intend.
beats.tele: When is `ORIG_HEAD` acceptable? Only as the very next command after the operation you want to undo, and only if that operation writes it. `git cherry-pick` doesn't. A commit doesn't. So a rebase followed by one commit, or a cherry-pick at any time, leaves `ORIG_HEAD` pointing somewhere you didn't intend.

beats.text: Failure modes: recipes that count parents, such as git reset --hard HEAD~1 to "undo the last merge". After a true merge, HEAD~1 is the previous tip of the branch. After a fast-forward, there is no merge commit, and HEAD~1 is the previous commit of the branch that was merged.
beats.tele: Failure modes: recipes that count parents, such as `git reset --hard HEAD~1` to "undo the last merge". After a true merge, `HEAD~1` is the previous tip of the branch. After a fast-forward, there is no merge commit, and `HEAD~1` is the previous commit of the branch that was merged.

beats.text: Keep the picture from last time: the commits are boxes that never left the vault, and each accident put a card in the wrong place.
beats.tele: Keep the picture from last time: the commits are boxes that never left the vault, and each accident put a card in the wrong place.

beats.text: Today add one refinement. Each branch has its own ledger page, and HEAD has a diary. The ledger page of a branch answers "where was this card yesterday". The diary answers "where did I walk". ORIG_HEAD is a sticky note with one box number and no heading: it doesn't say which card it was copied from, or when.
beats.tele: Today add one refinement. Each branch has its own ledger page, and HEAD has a diary. The ledger page of a branch answers "where was this card yesterday". The diary answers "where did I walk". `ORIG_HEAD` is a sticky note with one box number and no heading: it doesn't say which card it was copied from, or when.

beats.text: Try it now, on paper. Thirty seconds: draw a branch of three commits, then the same branch after a rebase. Do three of those commits exist now, or six? Say it out loud.
beats.tele: Try it now, on paper. Thirty seconds: draw a branch of three commits, then the same branch after a rebase. Do three of those commits exist now, or six? Say it out loud.

beats.text: Six. The model breaks in one place worth saying: a rebase doesn't move boxes. It builds new boxes with new numbers and leaves the old ones behind. Undoing a rebase means pointing the card back at the old boxes, and anything committed after the rebase sits on the new ones.
beats.tele: Six. The model breaks in one place worth saying: a rebase doesn't move boxes. It builds new boxes with new numbers and leaves the old ones behind. Undoing a rebase means pointing the card back at the old boxes, and anything committed after the rebase sits on the new ones.

beats.text: In four of the five, the repair line contains commits that existed all along. Only the names moved.
beats.tele: In four of the five, the repair line contains commits that existed all along. Only the names moved.

beats.text: Six commits ahead of the release branch where three belong.
beats.tele: Six commits ahead of the release branch where three belong.

beats.text: A commit was added after the rebase, so ORIG_HEAD isn't the answer. Read the branch reflog. Predict which entry is the tip from before the rebase. Say it out loud. I'll wait.
beats.tele: A commit was added after the rebase, so `ORIG_HEAD` isn't the answer. Read the branch reflog. Predict which entry is the tip from before the rebase. Say it out loud. I'll wait.

beats.text: The entry below "rebase (finish)": hotfix/judge-timeout@{2}, which is eb1f140. Anchor it, and anchor the present state too.
beats.tele: The entry below "rebase (finish)": `hotfix/judge-timeout@{2}`, which is `eb1f140`. Anchor it, and anchor the present state too.

beats.text: Two refs now hold the two versions of the branch. Nothing can be lost by what follows. Move only the commit that was made after the rebase onto the old tip.
beats.tele: Two refs now hold the two versions of the branch. Nothing can be lost by what follows. Move only the commit that was made after the rebase onto the old tip.

beats.text: Three commits on release/1.4 again: the two old ones with their old IDs, and "Log judge latency" as 13305ef. A wrong rebase is repaired with a correct rebase.
beats.tele: Three commits on `release/1.4` again: the two old ones with their old IDs, and "Log judge latency" as `13305ef`. A wrong rebase is repaired with a correct rebase.

beats.text: Read the word "Fast-forward".
beats.tele: Read the word "Fast-forward".

beats.text: Three work-in-progress commits are on main, and there is no merge commit.
beats.tele: Three work-in-progress commits are on `main`, and there is no merge commit.

beats.text: ORIG_HEAD..HEAD lists what the merge brought in. The merge was the last command and merge writes the slot, so ORIG_HEAD is valid here.
beats.tele: `ORIG_HEAD..HEAD` lists what the merge brought in. The merge was the last command and merge writes the slot, so `ORIG_HEAD` is valid here.

beats.text: --keep and not --hard. The experiment branch still exists. Only main moved back.

beats.text: Five mistakes to watch for.
beats.tele: Five mistakes to watch for.

beats.text: git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD after a cherry-pick, or a few commands after a rebase. Root cause: ORIG_HEAD is one slot written by reset, merge, rebase and am; it holds a value from an earlier operation, possibly on another branch.
beats.tele: `git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` after a cherry-pick, or a few commands after a rebase. Root cause: `ORIG_HEAD` is one slot written by reset, merge, rebase and am; it holds a value from an earlier operation, possibly on another branch.

beats.text: "Undo the last merge" with HEAD~1. Root cause: a fast-forward creates no merge commit, so HEAD~1 is a commit of the merged branch, not the previous tip.
beats.tele: "Undo the last merge" with `HEAD~1`. Root cause: a fast-forward creates no merge commit, so `HEAD~1` is a commit of the merged branch, not the previous tip.

beats.text: Resetting a rebased branch to its old tip when work was added afterwards. Root cause: the new commit sits on the rebased commits; anchor both tips and transplant the new commit with --onto.
beats.tele: Resetting a rebased branch to its old tip when work was added afterwards. Root cause: the new commit sits on the rebased commits; anchor both tips and transplant the new commit with `--onto`.

beats.text: Moving main back before copying the misplaced commits. Root cause: after the reset only the reflog names them; copy first, remove second.
beats.tele: Moving `main` back before copying the misplaced commits. Root cause: after the reset only the reflog names them; copy first, remove second.

beats.text: Rewinding a shared branch to remove a pushed merge or pick. Root cause: others have the commits and will bring them back or diverge; add a revert instead.
beats.tele: Rewinding a shared branch to remove a pushed merge or pick. Root cause: others have the commits and will bring them back or diverge; add a revert instead.

It closes with the check that would have prevented the incident, which is one read-only command.
